reason: E1 supports that Cr2O3 is a desirable protective oxide and that its absence can lead to Mn-rich oxide formation, but it does not address the effect of grain refinement or increased reactive element content. E2 directly supports that grain refinement via laser cladding provides high grain-boundary density acting as fast diffusion paths for Al and Cr, accelerating protective scale formation, but it attributes the superior performance to a synergistic effect including Y addition, not solely to increased Cr/Al and grain refinement as the hypothesis claims. premises: Increasing reactive element (Cr, Al) content promotes protective oxide formation
Refining microstructure (increasing grain-boundary density) accelerates protective oxide formation
Grain boundaries act as fast diffusion paths for reactive elements to the surface
Without sufficient reactive elements or grain-boundary density, Mn-rich non-protective oxides form
